title: The canonical polynomial map to the symmetric algebra of a projective conormal module has free conormal
statement: Let R and A be commutative rings with an R-algebra structure on A, and P a finite polynomial presentation of A with n variables and m relations [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], over the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let N be the conormal of this presentation. Let M be a projective A-module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], equipped with an A-linear equivalence e : N ≃ M. Write C = Sym_A(M) [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property], with any R-algebra structure compatible with R → A → C. For each relation r_j of P put z_j = e(class(r_j)). Let f : R[t_1,…,t_{n+m}] → C send the first n variables to the images of the n chosen generators of A, and the last m variables to ι(z_j). Then, for J = ker(f), its conormal J/J² is free over R[t]/J [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. The indexing includes n = 0 and m = 0, and R, A, and M may lie in different universes.

source.place: Proof of Lemma Tag 07CE, lines 357–414, at a = 1; polynomial surjection and equation-sequence. Online source checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07CE.

proof.text: Put I=P.ker and B=R[x]/I. The identity on conormal representatives gives the semilinear equivalence conormalQuotientEquiv from I.Cotangent to P.toExtension.Cotangent over P.quotientEquiv. Its scalar compatibility is proved by quotient induction, algebraMap_smul and Extension.Cotangent.val_smul'. Composing with e and applying Module.Projective.of_equiv to the inverse gives projectivity of I.Cotangent over B.

Define relation elements z in I and q by Pi.basisFun.constr. The basis evaluation formula gives q(Pi.single j 1)=I.toCotangent(z j). Define the literal polynomial ring map phi with eval₂Hom and the reduced map alpha with aeval. Their values on constants and variables are the required ones, by eval₂Hom_C, eval₂Hom_X' and aeval_X. Apply Algebra.symmetric_projective_presentation_conormal to these data and P.span_range_relation_eq_ker. Use its two final linear equivalences to transfer the freeness of Fin m → Sym_B(I.Cotangent) first to the tensor product and then to (Extension.ofSurjective phi hphi).Cotangent.

Apply symmetric_conormal_presentation_transport with the literal map's surjectivity. It supplies a scalar ring equivalence and a semilinear equivalence from the requested kernel conormal to the literal extension conormal. Apply Module.Free.of_equiv to the inverse of that semilinear equivalence. This proves exactly the stated Module.Free proposition, including all universes and empty-index cases.

proof_origin.place: Equation (16.3.1.1) and projective splitting at a=1; Lean application of the existing literal-quotient theorem with a separate presentation-transport lemma.

lean.statement:
theorem symmetric_conormal_free_presentation
    {R : Type u} {A : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    {n m : ℕ} (P : Algebra.Presentation R A (Fin n) (Fin m))
    (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Projective A M]
    (e : P.toExtension.Cotangent ≃ₗ[A] M)
    [Algebra R (SymmetricAlgebra A M)] [IsScalarTower R A (SymmetricAlgebra A M)] :
    let x : Fin m → M := fun j ↦ e (Extension.Cotangent.mk
      ⟨P.relation j, P.relation_mem_ker j⟩)
    let f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + m)) R →ₐ[R] SymmetricAlgebra A M :=
      MvPolynomial.aeval (fun i ↦ Sum.elim
        (fun j ↦ algebraMap A (SymmetricAlgebra A M) (P.val j))
        (fun j ↦ SymmetricAlgebra.ι A M (x j)) (finSumFinEquiv.symm i))
    Module.Free (MvPolynomial (Fin (n + m)) R ⧸ RingHom.ker f.toRingHom)
      (RingHom.ker f.toRingHom).Cotangent
